# Kybl: the fast S3 browser for your desktop

Kybl is a free desktop app for macOS, Windows and Linux that works with any S3-compatible object storage. Browse, upload, download, share and sync files on Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Hetzner Object Storage, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces, MinIO and Ceph. Website: https://kybl.app/

## Connect to any S3-compatible storage

Pick a provider preset, paste your access key and you're in. Kybl fills in the endpoint and region, explains each provider's quirks (for example, Hetzner keys cannot list all buckets, so you enter the bucket name) and can test the connection before saving. Path-style addressing is available for MinIO and self-hosted servers.

Secret keys are stored in the operating system keychain: the macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager or a Secret Service (GNOME Keyring, KWallet) on Linux. They are never written to a file.

## Features

- Thumbnails in a blink: JPEGs use the photo's embedded EXIF thumbnail, read from only the first 256 KB. Other images are resized once. All thumbnails are cached on disk, so a folder you've seen opens instantly.
- Previews without downloading: images, video, audio, PDF and text open in the details panel next to size, date and the full key.
- Drag, drop, done: upload files or whole folders by dragging from Finder or Explorer. Large files use multipart upload.
- A transfer queue that talks: speed and time left for every upload and download, with cancel and retry.
- Share links in one click: presigned URLs valid for 1 hour, 1 day or 7 days, or copy the s3:// URI. Nothing has to be made public.
- Huge folders, still snappy: lazy paging keeps folders with 100,000+ objects smooth; search looks through every subfolder.
- File operations: download files or folders, delete, rename files and folders, create folders, move items.
- Keyboard first: Cmd+F search, Cmd+A select all, Cmd+R refresh, arrow keys to move, Backspace to go up a folder, Delete to delete.
- Light and dark appearance that follows the system.

## Folder sync

Point a local folder at a bucket (or a prefix inside one) and choose a direction: upload to the bucket or download from it. Kybl watches for changes on a schedule, skips files that match ignore rules (such as node_modules or .DS_Store) and keeps syncing from the menu bar when the window is closed. All folders can be paused from the menu bar icon. Errors are shown in plain words with the fix, for example "AccessDenied: this key cannot list objects in static-assets".

## Download

- macOS: Apple Silicon and Intel builds
- Windows: 64-bit installer
- Linux: AppImage, .deb or .rpm

On first launch on a Mac, open System Settings > Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway (the app is signed but not yet notarized). On Windows, if SmartScreen warns, click More info > Run anyway.

## FAQ

Q: Which storage providers does Kybl work with?
A: Any S3-compatible storage: Amazon S3, Cloudflare R2, Hetzner Object Storage, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces, MinIO, Ceph and other S3 servers.

Q: Is Kybl free?
A: Yes. Kybl is a free download. You use your own bucket and pay your storage provider as usual.

Q: Where are my access keys stored?
A: In the operating system keychain. They are never written to a file, and Kybl talks to your storage directly.

Q: Can Kybl sync a folder with a bucket?
A: Yes, in either direction, with ignore rules, and it keeps running from the menu bar.

Q: Does Kybl handle very large files and folders?
A: Yes: multipart uploads for large files, paged loading for huge folders and recursive search.
